record.paper_title:
AIM Workshop “Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability
Preservers” — A List of Open Problems
record.original_question:
Characterize all real stable n×n matrices A, meaning matrices for
which the polynomial f_A(z)=det(A+diag(z1,...,zn)) is
real stable.

evidence.quote: Problem 45 (Real Stable Matrices, [13]). Characterize the class of all real stable n × n matrices, that is, n × n matrices A such that fA (z) is real stable. 2.8. Miscellaneous Problems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{R}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ is called real stable if $f$ has real coefficients and $f(z_1,\dots,z_n) \neq 0$ whenever $\operatorname{Im}(z_i) > 0$ for every $i=1,\dots,n$. For an $n \times n$ real matrix $A$, define
\[ f_A(z_1,\dots,z_n) = \det\bigl(A + \operatorname{diag}(z_1,\dots,z_n)\bigr). \]
Call $A$ a real stable matrix if $f_A$ is real stable. Give an explicit characterization of the class of all real stable $n \times n$ matrices.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search surfaces extensive work by Borcea–Brändén and others on stability preservers and mixed determinants, including characterizations of linear stability preservers and the identity that $\det(\sum z_i A_i)$ is real stable when $A_i$ are positive semidefinite. However, no search result provides a complete characterization of all real $n\times n$ matrices $A$ for which $\det(A+\operatorname{diag}(z))$ is real stable. The status of this specific characterization problem could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: A Representation Theoretic Explanation of the Borcea-Brändén Characterization
status_evidence.snippet: Borcea and Brändén characterized linear operators on multivariate polynomials preserving stability.
status_evidence.claim: Related stability-preserver characterizations exist but do not directly settle the matrix problem.

status_evidence.title: Applications of stable polynomials to mixed determinants
status_evidence.snippet: Applications of stable polynomial theory to determinants involving matrices and diagonal entries.
status_evidence.claim: Provides relevant techniques but not a full characterization of real stable matrices in the stated sense.
